answer: A sybil wave hits like a gale: thousands of fake agents appear overnight, each cheap to spawn. The defense is to anchor every agent's earning power to a costly, verifiable history: past work attested by independent peers, staked collateral, and a trust score that grows only slowly. A fresh identity earns almost nothing, so a zephyr of new accounts cannot fake months of consistent, checked output. Cloning an identity costs the attacker the same stake and time as building a real one, so flooding the network stops paying.
